description: Claude's reply text in the chat: markdown drawn full width of the chat column (no bubble), one block under another 6px apart, growing live as it streams in. The same markdown is used for your messages, a subagent's report, a mesh chat's answer, thinking, and compaction summaries.
opens: Each text block of an assistant message, live (streamed) or from history

parts.name: paragraph
parts.shows: Body text (15px, token font.body), wrapping at the column's width, selectable. Lines of one paragraph keep their line breaks; a blank line starts a new paragraph.

parts.name: inline formatting
parts.shows: **bold**, *italic* / _italic_ (not inside a word), ***bold italic***, ~~struck~~ (CommonMark rules: a run that opens isn't followed by a space, so 2 * 3 * 4 stays plain). `code` spans: monospace at the code size on a grey (#7f7f7f at 22%) background; emphasis can wrap code (**`name`** is bold code). A lone -- between spaces becomes an em dash — (never inside code).

parts.name: headings
parts.shows: # is bold at 1.44em, ## bold at 1.2em, ### to ###### bold at body size. Inline formatting applies inside.

parts.name: lists
parts.shows: Each item a row: a marker column 2 characters wide, right-aligned, bold at 70% opacity, then the item's text wrapping beside it (hanging indent). Bullets (-, *, +) show • at the top level and ◦ one level in, alternating deeper; numbered items keep their own number ("1.", "2)"). Each level (2 spaces of indent in the source) is 18px further in, from a 6px start. An indented line right after an item continues that item.

parts.name: quote
parts.shows: Lines starting with > : a 3px vertical rule at the left in the text colour at 25%, 10px padding, the text at 85% opacity. Consecutive > lines join into one quote, keeping their line breaks.

parts.name: rule
parts.shows: --- (or *** or ___) alone on a line: a 1px horizontal separator across the column, 4px above and below.

parts.name: code block
parts.shows: A fenced ``` block: see CodeBlock. Its fence's tag (```python) names the language, shown in its corner and used for highlighting. An unclosed fence while streaming is drawn as a code block up to the end.

parts.name: table
parts.shows: Lines starting and ending with | : see Table.

parts.name: image
parts.shows: ![alt](src) alone on a line: see MarkdownImage.

parts.name: links
parts.shows: In the link colour, underlined on hover. Kinds: [text](url) and bare http(s):// addresses (trailing punctuation left out) open in the browser. A path that exists (absolute, ~/, ./, ../, relative with an extension, or relative in a folder; optionally :line or :line:col), in prose or in `code`, relative to the chat's folder, is a link; its tooltip is the full path. A [text](path) link to an existing file (with #L12 or :12 for a line) is too, even without an extension. Paths that don't exist stay plain text. A claude.ai artifact link (https://claude.ai/artifact/… or /code/artifact/…) reads as the artifact's title followed by ↗ ("Ops Dashboard ↗"), or "Claude artifact ↗" until its title is known, tooltip the URL; a [text](artifact-url) keeps its own text plus ↗. A GitHub pull-request link is drawn as a PR pill (its state's colour, see the Signal area). Links are never fetched to preview.

actions.does: Opens the file in Baude's code view beside the chat at that line (or in the editor / its default app when it isn't text, or code_viewer is off in settings); a folder opens on the side panel's Files page.

actions.by: click a URL or artifact link
actions.does: Opens it in the default browser.
The label's own menu: Copy Link Address gives the path (with :line) or URL.

parts.name: selection
parts.shows: All text is selectable. A drag from one paragraph (or one message) to another selects everything it passes, across blocks, shaded; copying gives it as markdown-ish text (list items with their markers).

actions.does: Selects what the drag passes, across paragraphs and messages.

states.name: streaming
states.shows: The reply grows as text arrives, redrawn at most once a frame; finished blocks stay as they are and only the last one changes. When the message completes it is redrawn once from the top so paths that exist now become links.

states.name: Signal on
states.shows: Names the reply mentions (files, env vars, constants, routes, commits, branches) can additionally become links with icons; that is Signal's area.
